audit.whatIsWrong: Six of seven full-layer rows read 'Skill' while the content layer (and packet.levelChart) read Skill/Yone/Galio/Galio/Galio/Yone/Yone, and every why was the generic Galio template.
audit.why: The content layer matches the packet exactly, so the full layer is the broken one. Real spikes: his level 2 (two Mortal Steel stacks dash and knock up), your levels 3-6, his first crit item, then the late side lane.
audit.corrected: Six sides moved onto the packet/content verdicts, ratings adjusted and all seven whys rewritten, as one atomic group. No win[] edits are needed — the content layer already holds the correct values.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page never named a single Yone ability (packet defect) and, where the content layer did describe his kit, it described the wrong abilities: it called Soul Unbound (E) a 'dash-in' with 'E-mark resets' he could 'flash away', and it claimed Winds of War knocks him up.
audit.why: Riot's text: Soul Unbound sends his spirit out of his body and forces it back — it is not a dash and there is no mark on you. The dash and knockup live on Mortal Steel (Q) at two stacks. Galio's Q is two windblasts converging into a tornado; the knockup is Justice Punch (E).
audit.corrected: Early, mid, late, spikes and the wants lists now name Mortal Steel, Spirit Cleave, Soul Unbound and Fate Sealed correctly, and the knockup is attributed to Justice Punch.

audit.why: Soul Unbound is 22/19/16/13/10 and Spirit Cleave is a flat 14 — the gap between 22s at rank 1 and 10s at rank 5 is the whole shape of the lane.
audit.corrected: Both numbers written in alongside Shield of Durand's 18s.

edits.before: Best wave: a Q-cleared middle wave that keeps your R timer flexible — Galio waves are about being free to leave. Autopilot shoving buys ganks.
edits.after: Best wave: a middle wave you can leave — match his clear so the R timer stays free and the roam is always available. Worst wave: a wave you shove into his tower while Soul Unbound is up at 22s and he takes a free reset off it. Crash timing: crash before you roam — Yone chases waves, not champions, so the lane holds itself while you are gone.

edits.before: Level 1-2 is a coinflip: Yone's E dash-in can catch you before you have Q/W/E all up, and his Level 2 all-in with an early point in Q punishes any greedy trade. From Level 3 onward you out-scale the skirmish — Winds of War knocks him up if he tries to walk through minions, and Shield of Durand plus Justice Punch lets you win extended trades he can't escape from without flashing his E away.
edits.after: Level 1-2 is a coinflip: two Mortal Steel stacks dash him in with a knockup before you have Q/W/E all up, and his Level 2 all-in punishes any greedy trade. From Level 3 onward you out-scale the skirmish — Justice Punch is the knockup here, not your Q, and Shield of Durand plus that dash wins extended trades he cannot leave unless Soul Unbound is already up.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are yours to push: freeze the wave slightly outside your tower range so his E-mark reset windows shrink, and poke him down with Q before he can close. The moment he hits 6, respect his all-in — Yone's ult is a teleport gap-closer that ignores your knockup timing if you're out of position, so hold Hero's Entrance in reserve to flip back onto him rather than dying to the double-engage.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are yours to push: hold the wave slightly outside your tower range so his Spirit Cleave shield is spent on minions, and poke him down with Q before he can close. The moment he hits 6, respect the all-in — Fate Sealed blinks him 1000 units behind the last champion in the line and drags everyone back with him, so hold Hero's Entrance to answer it rather than dying to the double-engage.

edits.before: Once Yone finishes his first crit item (typically Kraken/IE rush) his all-in burst outpaces your sustain trades, and by full build he can solo-carry skirmishes your tank kit can't out-damage. Group as a team, force him to fight into your W shield and R engage rather than dueling him 1v1 in a side lane, and treat his ult as a flank threat that needs vision to counter, not a fair fight to take alone.

The dash and knockup are Mortal Steel at two stacks. It also claimed Winds of War knocks him up; the knockup is Justice Punch. All of that is corrected.
